schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The read of `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`, written once for the whole corpus. Two functions: `cgroup_of(pid='self')` returns the unified (v2) hierarchy path for a pid, or None; `parse(raw)` is the same parse over the file's text, so a proof can pin the behaviour without a live pid. It answers ONE question — where in the unified hierarchy does this process live — and answers nothing else: containment, residency kind, lifetime and liveness are JUDGEMENTS and stay with the probe that makes them (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/probes/does_the_heartbeat_outlive_its_caller.py). None is a real answer, never an error: a v1-only host, a pid that exited between the listing and the read, and a container with no unified hierarchy all land there, and each is a fact about the world (Law 7 — the lack is named by the caller that reports it, never swallowed here into a plausible default). The kernel's ' (deleted)' suffix is dropped, because a cgroup removed out from under a still-living process is exactly what a killed caller's scope looks like for the moment between the kill and the last exit, and the path is still the identity.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM: the same eight-line parse had grown in three places, and nobody could have told you which one was right. Measured 2026-09-08 — `cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/probes/does_the_heartbeat_outlive_its_caller.py`, `cairn/devices/cc/probes/memory_curve.py` and `launchers/proofs/test_superclaude_memory_scope.py` each opened the file and each looped for the '0::' line on its own account. Two of the three had already lost the ' (deleted)' handling, so a killed caller's scope compared unequal to itself. That is Law 1's defect exactly: a settled answer re-derived, three times, silently. The corpus DID carry a check against it — arm 6 of launchers/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py censuses every python read of the path and demands exactly one — and it did not fire, because its seal was directory-scoped over launchers/ and the two later voyages that grew the readers never touched that directory. WHY A TOOL AND NOT A SHARED PROBE: the readers sit on two different devices, and devices do not import each other (RULED — only db_domain crosses). A complete primitive with users rather than an owner IS a tool (Law 6); this one is pure, stateless, and has nothing of its own to gate.
invoke: `from cairn.tools.cgroup.cgroup import cgroup_of` — or `parse` when you already hold the file's text. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/cgroup/proofs/test_cgroup.py`. There is no CLI: the answer is a string a caller composes, not a report anyone reads.
entry: EXTRACTED 2026-09-08, not written fresh — the bytes are the ground_loop residency probe's `cgroup_of`, which was the one of the three spellings that was complete (it alone dropped the ' (deleted)' suffix, and its header already claimed to be THE one reader). The probe keeps its judgements (`is_descendant`, `residency`, `alive`) and composes this for the read. `parse` is the one addition, split out so the behaviour can be proved over text instead of over whatever cgroup the test runner happens to live in.
state_and_history: NONE, and none is coming. It is a pure function over a kernel file: no cache, no counter, no journal. There is no state.json or history.json beside this charter, and their absence is this component's ordinary resting state rather than a missing file. Should it ever come to carry state, that state berths under the holder that assembled it (ruling 2026-08-14-tools-and-machines-remember-under-their-holder), never here.
filed_edges: (a) THE CENSUS THAT GUARDS THIS LIVES IN A PROOF UNDER ANOTHER COMPONENT'S SEAL. Arm 6 of launchers/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py is what reds a fourth reader, and it is sealed directory-scoped over launchers/ — which is precisely why it slept through the two voyages that grew readers two and three. Until the census fires from somewhere the whole corpus's seals reach (a build_inspector sieve is the obvious home), a new re-spelling is caught only when someone happens to run that proof. OPEN.

(b) NO v1 FALLBACK, ON PURPOSE. Only the '0::' unified line is read; a v1-only host gets None. Every consumer today runs on this laptop's cgroup v2, and inventing a v1 path nothing exercises would be a hollow branch (Law 8). If a v1 host ever matters it arrives as a measurement, not as a guess.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_cgroup.py under the tester. Durability gate: committed + pushed. Census gate: arm 6 of launchers/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py must name THIS module as the corpus's sole python reader of the path.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a second file in the corpus opens `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` from python — the census in arm 6 is the instrument, and this is the failure the component exists to end; (2) `parse` returns a path carrying the kernel's ' (deleted)' suffix, or drops a legitimate trailing segment that merely resembles it; (3) a missing, unreadable or v1-only source raises instead of returning None; (4) a non-unified line ('1:name=systemd:/x') is read as the answer; (5) this module grows a judgement — containment, lifetime, liveness — that belongs to the probe, which would make it a machine wearing a tool's name. WRONG INTENT: if the corpus still shows one reader a year on because nobody else ever needed a cgroup, the extraction bought nothing the probe's own header did not already claim — the value is in the SECOND and THIRD consumers composing it, and today there are exactly two.
proof: proofs/test_cgroup.py — the parse pinned over synthetic text in both directions (a unified line found, a v1-only file returning None, the ' (deleted)' marker stripped and a path merely ending in similar bytes left alone), the live read pinned against the kernel's own file for this process, an exited pid pinned as None rather than as an exception, and the corpus census pinned so a fourth reader reds here too and not only in launchers/.
owner: A TOOL HAS USERS, NOT AN OWNER (Law 6). Its users today: the ground_loop residency probe, cc's memory_curve probe, and the superclaude memory-scope proof. CC writes the code and proofs; Akien owns the design.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel — one parse, written once, is the whole point)
Law 6 (a tool has users, not an owner — which is what makes this the right rung for code two devices need)
Law 7 (None is a named lack, never a plausible default)
I-borrow-patterns-cite-dont-graft (the bytes came from the probe and the entry says so)
provenance: Born 2026-09-08 out of a red, not out of a plan: the re-seal sweep re-ran launchers/proofs/test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller.py for the first time since 6ae83e7, and arm 6's census reported three readers where the criterion allows one. The two extra readers arrived with tickets 4d96964532c2 (superclaude-per-instance-memory-max) and a6cf55a6dd6d (the-memory-curve-is-recorded-not-eyeballed), each of which passed its own gates.
learns: It does not, and it should not — it is a parse of a kernel file with a fixed format. The learning that surrounds it belongs to the census (edge (a)): what the corpus needs to learn is not how to read a cgroup but how to notice the fourth place someone re-derives it.
how_it_learns: IT DOES NOT LEARN, because there is nothing here for evidence to change: the '0::' line's format is the kernel's, not a parameter. The feedback loop that matters runs one level up, at the census in arm 6 — every new reader it catches is evidence about whether extraction alone is enough physics or whether the check has to move somewhere the whole corpus's seals reach (edge (a)).
